clue.text: He trades in Mercedes, 50% less than new

indicators.note: taking fifty per cent away from the eight-letter car name leaves only its front half
new signals that the word than is made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A car dealer offers a Mercedes at half the price of a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% less' keeps the first half of MERCEDES, MERC; 'new' rearranges THAN into HANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a dealer, someone whose business is buying and selling goods.

clue.text: Capture in French bunker

parts.note: the French word for in is en
a golf bunker is a sand trap

explanation.surface: A French bunker is used to take prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf bunker is a sand-filled hazard, also called a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch or snare, a synonym of capture as a verb.

clue.text: Central heating off apparently!

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating in property ads
feeling off means feeling unwell, or ill

explanation.surface: With the heating turned off, the house feels cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a house with the central heating off has a cold feel to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a coldness in the air, just what you notice when the radiators are not running.

clue.text: A cut restricts meagre grant

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the word for cut holds the word for meagre inside it

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as with a boil
low means small or meagre, as in a low wage

explanation.surface: A reduction limits an already stingy financial grant.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a sum of money granted regularly, such as pocket money or a benefit.

clue.text: Down-trodden machine-worker

parts.note: reads as an oppressed factory hand, but describes a foot pedal that is pressed downward to drive a machine such as a sewing machine or lathe

explanation.surface: An oppressed factory worker toils at the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that powers a machine when pushed down repeatedly.

clue.text: Swindle uncovered in the courts

definitions.meaning: a dishonest scheme to make money, a fraud
the strung bat used on tennis or squash courts, taken out of its protective cover for play

explanation.surface: A fraud is exposed during legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law courts, but here they are tennis or squash courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a con or scam; the same word names the bat swung in tennis and squash.

clue.text: Show travelled round

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle
a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: A show went on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of cowboy skills such as bronco riding, a kind of show.

clue.text: Eire faces new truce

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the words before it are formed into something different

explanation.surface: Ireland agrees to a fresh truce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the nine letters of EIRE FACES.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire is a halt in fighting agreed between sides, a synonym of truce.

clue.text: Should one see the dentist with it?

definitions.text: Should one see the dentist with it?

parts.words: Should one see the dentist with it?
parts.note: seems to ask whether a dental complaint calls for a visit, but plays on the idea of a tooth you see with, the canine below the eye

explanation.surface: A patient wonders whether a dental problem warrants a trip to the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyetooth is a canine in the upper jaw, so named because it sits directly below the eye.

clue.text: When one chooses a woven fabric

definitions.meaning: as and when one pleases, freely
an article plus twill, a cloth woven with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Someone picks a woven cloth whenever they like.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the letters give A TWILL: twill is a cloth with a diagonal weave.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever you please; twill is a strong diagonally ribbed cloth.

clue.text: Blank sheet to finish a learned discourse

parts.note: end and finish are synonyms
an academic paper is a scholarly essay or treatise

explanation.surface: An academic needs a fresh sheet to complete a scholarly article.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the plain leaf pasted inside the cover of a book, a blank page.

clue.text: Public building due to be consecrated

parts.note: a town hall or village hall is a public building
owed means due, as of a debt

explanation.surface: A town hall is scheduled to be blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy, a synonym of consecrated.

clue.text: Mineral almost exhausted in this state

parts.note: ore is rock from which a mineral or metal is extracted

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for exhausted is dropped

parts.note: gone means used up or exhausted

explanation.surface: A mining region is running short of its mineral wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from GONE, leaving GON.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state of the USA in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Handy aids to solving crime

parts.note: handy seems to mean useful, but literally these traces come from the hand and help detectives identify a culprit

explanation.surface: Detectives value useful tools for cracking cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks left by the ridged skin of the fingertips are used by police to identify suspects.

clue.text: Faults of flimsy neckwear

parts.note: frail means weak or flimsy
ties are worn around the neck

explanation.surface: Someone points out the defects in some cheap, thin neckties.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailties are moral weaknesses or failings, a synonym of faults.

clue.text: Added figures for golfers?

parts.note: plus is the word for added in arithmetic
fours are numerals, figures

explanation.surface: Golfers' scorecards show numbers totted up.
explanation.walkthrough: These baggy knee-length trousers were traditionally worn on the golf course, hence 'for golfers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus fours are loose breeches gathered below the knee, classic golfing attire.

clue.text: Blend of tea I sold apart from the rest

indicators.note: a blend of tea mixes leaves together, so the letters of these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tea merchant sells a special blend.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means set apart and alone, separated from others.

clue.text: Always part of a Houdini contract?

definitions.text: Always part of a Houdini contract?

parts.words: Always part of a Houdini contract?
parts.note: a contract provision letting a party get out of its obligations, which an escapologist would naturally insist on

explanation.surface: The great escapologist's agreements always include one particular term.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape clause is a contract provision that releases a party from obligations under stated conditions, apt for the famous escapologist.

clue.text: Permit excessive behaviour?

definitions.meaning: an official document giving permission, such as a driving permit

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether bad behaviour is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is an official permit; the word also means excessive freedom or lack of restraint.

clue.text: Disloyal unit I left with regret

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I goes from the word unit

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A traitorous soldier walks out on his regiment and is sorry afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' takes the I out of UNIT, giving UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue can mean unfaithful, as in a lover who is untrue, a synonym of disloyal.

clue.text: One taking Kelly around Yorkshire moor

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of the name are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone takes Kelly for a walk across a Yorkshire moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like 'taking Kelly round the moor' but rearranges the name (LKLEY). Ilkley Moor in West Yorkshire is famous from the folk song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilkley Moor is the stretch of moorland above the spa town of Ilkley, in Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: New York backing gets university knock-out inclusion for Canadian region

indicators.note: an inclusion is something placed within, so the other letters go inside
backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation for the city is read in reverse

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout

explanation.surface: A New York investor's backing secures a university a stake in a Canadian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads like financial support but turns the city's initials round (YN); 'inclusion' then sets the university and boxing abbreviations inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yukon is a territory in north-western Canada, famous for its gold rush.

clue.text: Diner imbibes fine new coffee ingredient

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in or drink, so the word for diner holds the other letters

parts.note: a café is an informal diner

indicators.note: new signals the letters of fine are given a new order

explanation.surface: A diner serves coffee with a fine new blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diner' poses as a person eating but is the café; 'new' reworks fine as FEIN, which 'imbibes' places before the café's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is the stimulant found in coffee beans, one of its key chemical constituents.

clue.text: A bit above a walk-on part

definitions.meaning: a little more than usual, additional
a minor role in a film, usually a non-speaking crowd member

explanation.surface: An actor's walk-on role is a little better than nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, beyond the standard; an extra is a film actor with a tiny non-speaking role.

clue.text: Laid low by swindle in currency

indicators.note: in signals that the word for swindle sits within the word for currency

parts.note: the sen is a small unit of currency in Japan and parts of South-East Asia
a trick is a con or swindle

explanation.surface: Someone is ruined by a currency fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken means struck down by illness or misfortune, brought down.

clue.text: Recovery vessel — put out in it

indicators.note: in it means the rearranged letters go into the word for vessel

parts.note: an urn is a vessel, a vase or container

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of put are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A salvage ship is told to put out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recovery vessel' suggests a salvage ship, but recovery is the definition; 'out' reworks put as UPT, and 'in it' sets that inside the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement, as in an economic recovery.

clue.text: A famous man, but there's no airs about him

indicators.note: about signals that the phrase describing him is read the other way round

parts.note: side is British slang for pretension or airs, as in putting on side

explanation.surface: A celebrity is admired for being modest and unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about him' turns NO SIDE backwards. SIDE is old British slang for swagger or putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb, is a celebrated figure.

clue.text: Turn and sneer when trapped

indicators.note: to turn something is to change it about, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An animal snarls and turns when caught in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means caught in a snare, a synonym of trapped.
